name: transcribe-speech
summary: Transcribe speech to text from 16kHz mono audio using a real Whisper-tiny encoder-decoder transformer forward pass, gated on a Silero VAD speech-presence pre-check so it never hallucinates a transcript for non-speech audio.
description: Runs a real openai/whisper-tiny forward pass -- 80-channel log-mel spectrogram front end, a 2-conv1d/4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer encoder, a 4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer decoder with causal self-attention and cross-attention to the full encoder output, then greedy (argmax, no beam search) autoregressive decoding seeded with a fixed startoftranscript/English/transcribe/no-timestamps prompt -- an officially-sanctioned, documented minimal decoding path (HF's own generation_config.json ships this exact forced-token configuration for this model). New in 1.1.0: before running the (expensive) encoder/decoder at all, the input is scored by audio.detect-speech-segments' Silero VAD engine (registry#460, reused directly, not duplicated) in its own fixed 512-sample chunks; if no chunk anywhere in the clip clears a speech-probability threshold, the capability returns an empty transcript immediately. This fixes a real, observed failure mode in 1.0.0: Whisper has no notion of 'is this speech at all' and would confidently transcribe non-speech, non-silent audio (a tone, music, noise) as plausible-sounding text -- a synthetic sine wave came back as ' [MUSIC PLAYING]'. True silence was already handled by a cheap energy-threshold check; this closes the gap for non-silent non-speech audio. Not a KV-cached decoder: each step recomputes the full decoder stack over the token sequence so far, which is correctness-first and entirely tractable at this model's scale. Complements audio.detect-speech-segments (registry#460) directly (reuses its engine rather than merely being conceptually related to it): an app that already gates on 'is there speech in this clip' is a short step from 'what did it say', and this capability now performs that same check internally by default. Input is up to 30 seconds (480000 samples) of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; shorter clips are zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window (longer audio must be pre-chunked by the caller -- this capability does not chunk or stream). Known, documented limitations: output capped at 224 decoded tokens; English-only (language is forced, not detected -- non-English input transcribes as attempted English, once past the speech-presence gate); greedy single-hypothesis decoding, so exact wording (e.g. punctuation) can differ slightly from a beam-search reference without being wrong; the speech-presence gate is a presence check (any chunk clearing the threshold proceeds), not a duration/coverage measurement, so a clip that is mostly non-speech with one brief speech burst is still fully transcribed. Does not translate, diarize speakers, produce timestamps, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want spoken audio transcribed to text, so that I can search, summarize, or extract entities from what was said without a separate ASR service.
As a meeting organizer, I want silent or empty audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a hallucinated guess, so that gaps in a recording don't produce fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want a tone, music, or other non-speech-but-not-silent audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a confident hallucination, so that a recording's non-speech portions don't pollute a transcript with fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want an explicit model_unavailable status rather than a silent empty transcript when the artifact was built without its weight table, so that a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies up to 480000 (30s) samples of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; fewer than 30s of audio is zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window.

postconditions.description: Empty samples, or audio whose total energy is below a small fixed threshold, yields text="" rather than a hallucinated transcript.
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a text transcript in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input audio.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#477, highest-ROI follow-up identified from the post-#473 'Five Engines, What Next' downstream-capability review: gate audio.transcribe-speech's expensive Whisper forward pass on audio.detect-speech-segments' (#460) Silero VAD speech-presence check, fixing an observed hallucination-on-non-speech failure mode rather than a speculative improvement. Framed as a new minor version of this capability (one coherent 'transcribe speech, robustly' action) rather than a cross-capability workflow, which is out of this repo's scope (app-repo concern).

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/audio-transcribe-speech: 18 #[test] cases (the 14 from v1.0.0 plus 4 new for the VAD pre-check: max-speech-probability finite/bounded, deterministic, empty-input, and exact-chunk-multiple edge cases) against a synthetic WHSP1 fixture and audio-detect-speech-segments' own exposed VAD1 fixture_model() (registry#460's crate was split into a lib+bin so this capability can reuse its scoring engine directly rather than duplicating it -- the published audio.detect-speech-segments@1.0.0 contract/artifact is untouched by this source-only refactor); cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=98.45%, regions=98.64%. Verified empirically on real audio (not assumed): the real 11s JFK clip and its 1s excerpt transcribe identically to v1.0.0 (VAD correctly recognizes real speech on every chunk, so the gate never falsely blocks real speech); a synthetic sine tone that v1.0.0 hallucinated as ' [MUSIC PLAYING]' now correctly returns empty text; true silence still returns empty text via the unchanged, cheaper energy check. Threshold (max VAD speech probability across all 512-sample chunks in the clip must clear 0.5) verified against all three cases via the compiled wasm32-unknown-unknown --features full-model artifact under wasmtime, not just the Python/Rust source -- byte-for-byte match with the expected outputs in every case. License: same as v1.0.0 (dual-attested MIT/Apache-2.0 for Whisper-tiny; MIT for Silero VAD, already recorded on audio.detect-speech-segments).
